summary: Explains that since 2.22 no_log module options keep their real value in results (registered as a secret) instead of VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER, so later tasks can use it; very short values can over-mask and be guessed, so prefer longer values or the no_log keyword.
questions: Why can I now see the real password in a registered user module result?
Why is a short password masking random words in my output?

answer_card.title: Changes to the no_log module option
answer_card.answer_md:
Before 2.22, `no_log` options were replaced with `VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER`. Since 2.22 the real value stays in the result and is registered as a secret, so it's masked in output but usable later:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.user:
    name: deploy
    password: "{{ generated_hash }}"
  register: user_result
- ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - user_result.invocation.module_args.password == generated_hash
```

Very short values get masked inside unrelated words and can be guessed; prefer longer values or use the `no_log` task keyword.
